record.paper_title: Long time behaviour of one facilitated kinetically constrained models: results and open problems
record.context_brief: Exponential relaxation under an exponential-tail hypothesis
record.original_question: In the same one-dimensional FA-1f model on Z with infection density q in (0,1) and equilibrium measure π, suppose the initial law ν has exponentially decaying probability of containing no infected site in a centered interval, in the sense that there exists κ > 0 such that ν(no infected vertices in [−ℓ,ℓ]) = O(e^{−κℓ}) for all sufficiently large ℓ. Does this stronger nondegeneracy assumption imply that, for every q > 0, the convergence of local observables to equilibrium is exponentially fast in time?

evidence.quote: The next obvious question concerns the speed of relaxation to the reversible measure π under some condition on ν stronger than just the a.s. existence of some infection. Conjecture 2. If there exists κ > 0 such that ν(no infected vertices in [−ℓ, ℓ]) = O(e−κℓ) for all ℓ > 0 large enough then for all q > 0 the convergence in (1.1) is exponentially fast.
For the FA-1f process the constraint satisfies cx(η) = 1{ηx−1+ηx+1̸=2}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Fredrickson–Andersen one-spin facilitated (FA-1f) kinetically constrained Markov process on the one-dimensional lattice $\mathbb{Z}$ with parameter $q\in(0,1)$. The state space is $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$, where at each site $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ the value $\eta_x=1$ is interpreted as "infected" and $\eta_x=0$ as "healthy". The dynamics is a continuous-time Markov process with generator
$$ (\mathcal{L} f)(\eta) \;=\; \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}} c_x(\eta)\,\bigl[q\,(1-\eta_x) + (1-q)\,\eta_x\bigr]\,\bigl(f(\eta^x)-f(\eta)\bigr), $$
where $\eta^x$ denotes $\eta$ with the value at $x$ flipped, and the constraint is
$$ c_x(\eta) \;=\; \mathbf{1}\{\eta_{x-1}+\eta_{x+1}\neq 2\}, $$
i.e. site $x$ may flip only when at least one of its two nearest neighbours is healthy. The product Bernoulli measure $\pi=\mathrm{Ber}(q)^{\otimes\mathbb{Z}}$ is reversible.

Let $\nu$ be an initial probability measure on $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$, and write $\nu_t$ for the law at time $t\ge 0$ of the FA-1f process started from $\nu$. Assume there exists $\kappa>0$ such that
$$ \nu\bigl(\eta_x=0\ \text{for all}\ x\in[-\ell,\ell]\bigr) \;=\; O\!\left(e^{-\kappa\ell}\right) \qquad \text{as } \ell\to\infty. $$

Prove or disprove: under this assumption, for every $q\in(0,1)$ and every local function $f:\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}\to\mathbb{R}$, the convergence
$$ \mathbb{E}_{\nu_t}[f] \;\longrightarrow\; \pi(f) \qquad (t\to\infty) $$
takes place at an exponential rate in $t$; that is, there exist constants $C=C(f,\nu,q)<\infty$ and $\lambda=\lambda(f,\nu,q)>0$ such that
$$ \bigl|\mathbb{E}_{\nu_t}[f]-\pi(f)\bigr| \;\le\; C\,e^{-\lambda t} \qquad \text{for all } t\ge 0. $$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is explicitly listed as an open problem in a recent survey on the long-time behaviour of one-facilitated kinetically constrained models. Web search did not surface any work resolving the exponential-relaxation question for FA-1f under the exponential-tail nondegeneracy assumption on the initial law, so the problem appears to remain open.
